thread:
alex: Heads up — a couple of long GHA matrix jobs started failing mid-run with 401s from the Redwood API around 08:10 UTC. Jobs run ~45m. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

jamal: I got the alert from infra-bot :warning:. Can you paste the runner log snippet where the 401 happens?

alex: here's the tail from the job step that talks to the API — 401 right after an access token is used:
```
[2024-06-26T08:23:12Z] INFO request: POST /v1/generate
[2024-06-26T08:23:12Z] INFO auth: using access token from helper
[2024-06-26T08:23:13Z] ERROR 401 Unauthorized: invalid_token
[2024-06-26T08:23:13Z] DEBUG token_age: 00:14:37
```

maria: Are you impersonating a service account via gcloud from the runner? Is this the usual OIDC->impersonation flow or a cached JSON token?

alex: yep, we use a helper action (deploy-helper) that calls gcloud to generate a short-lived access token and then exports it to env for requests. Example command we run: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts generate-access-token \
  --impersonate-service-account=sa-deployer@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --format=json --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform --duration=900s
```

jamal: two likely things: 1) you're deliberately setting a tiny duration (900s = 15m) for least-privilege; long-running jobs hit expiry if refresh isn't scheduled. 2) the helper might cache the token and not refresh per matrix job. Can you paste the JSON output from generate-access-token (expireTime field)?

alex: pasted output from helper run (sanitized):
```
{"accessToken":"ya29...","expireTime":"2024-06-26T08:25:00Z"}
```

maria: that lines up — token expiry ~08:25 and job failed at 08:23 after ~14m of use. Two flavors of fixes: increase duration to 3600s (if org policy allows) or change helper to refresh at 50% of lifetime or on every job matrix cell start.

jamal: note on org policy: our IAM impersonation binding for the deployer SA has a sessionDuration constraint in the org that restricts max duration to 1h, but we explicitly requested 15m via --duration. If least-privilege wants short tokens, we must ensure runner refreshes them during long jobs.

infra-bot: Incident INC-1421 created and assigned to @jamal. https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-1421

alex: quick mitigation I pushed to the repo: add a step before API-heavy loops that reruns the helper every 10m (ugly but works). We'll revert when helper patched.

deploy-helper: Suggested patch: auto-refresh tokens in the helper with jitter; refresh_threshold_pct=50% by default. Will open PR.

maria: please also add a short KB entry explaining the interplay: token --duration vs org-level sessionDuration vs runner caching. We had similar flakes in a backfill last quarter.

jamal: I'll open the PR for the helper and add a repo-wide workflow change to call the helper per matrix cell start. Also will run a quick audit across repos for any helper usages that pass --duration <= 900s.

alex: thanks. For completeness, recording repro steps we used: 1) start a matrix job that runs ~40–50m and has a single generate-access-token at start with --duration=900s; 2) let job run until ~14m and observe 401 on subsequent requests; 3) rerun with helper refresh enabled to validate fix.

maria: perfect — marking as actionable. jamal, please ping #eng-runtime if you need an emergency exception to raise the allowed max duration for a specific SA. :thumbsup:

jamal: will do. PR and audit tickets incoming. :white_check_mark:
